scope: Bounded source-clause and named-bullet decomposition of Waves references 3.1–3.29P, visually checked on specification PDF pages 22–24 / printed 16–18. Linked teaching and assessment checks remain partial.
identifierPolicy: Requirement suffixes r1, r2, etc. are local editorial audit identifiers; only the parent reference is publisher-numbered.

parents.scopeNote: All five named units are tracked; conversions and selected examples do not establish complete unit fluency.

requirements.summary: Use degrees for wave and ray angles.
remainingChecks: Check angle-unit reading and normal-versus-surface references independently.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use hertz for frequency.
remainingChecks: Calibrate Hz/kHz/MHz conversions without confusing frequency and period.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use metres for wave distances.
remainingChecks: Check distance and wavelength prefixes in unfamiliar graph scales.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use metres per second for wave speed.
remainingChecks: Validate speed calculations with mixed distance/time prefixes.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use seconds for wave timing.
remainingChecks: Validate ms-to-s conversion and several-cycle measurements.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Classification compares vibration with energy-transfer direction, not the shape of a plotted trace.

requirements.summary: Explain transverse versus longitudinal vibration directions.
remainingChecks: Assess both wave types from unfamiliar diagrams and reject classification by trace shape.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: The five named quantities are separate local requirements under one publisher parent.

requirements.summary: Define amplitude.
remainingChecks: Check equilibrium-to-maximum distance rather than crest-to-trough height.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Define a wavefront.
remainingChecks: Add and validate a wavefront/propagation-direction diagram task.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Define frequency.
remainingChecks: Assess complete oscillations per second independently of wavelength.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Define wavelength.
remainingChecks: Check equivalent spatial points for longitudinal and transverse representations.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Define period.
remainingChecks: Assess one-cycle duration versus elapsed time for multiple cycles.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Energy and information transfer are both named; absence of net matter transfer is an explicit condition.

requirements.summary: Recognise that waves transfer energy and information.
remainingChecks: Validate an explanation linking a changing signal to transmitted information.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Distinguish wave transfer from overall transfer of matter.
remainingChecks: Assess local particle oscillation versus propagation in both wave types.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Know/use are local demand subdivisions of the supplied source relationship.

requirements.summary: Know v = fλ.
remainingChecks: Validate independent equation recall and quantity identification.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use v = fλ.
remainingChecks: Calibrate forward/inverse targets and prefix conversions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: The source asks use of frequency = 1/period.

requirements.summary: Calculate frequency or period using their reciprocal relationship.
remainingChecks: Validate inverse targets, scientific notation and multiple-cycle timing.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Sound and electromagnetic waves are explicit included contexts, not interchangeable source speeds.

requirements.summary: Apply wave relationships to sound.
remainingChecks: Review unfamiliar sound media and avoid assuming air speed universally.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Apply wave relationships to electromagnetic waves.
remainingChecks: Calibrate wavelength/frequency targets over realistic spectrum scales.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Source motion relative to the observer is required; the numerical Doppler formula is not specified.

requirements.summary: Explain observed frequency/wavelength changes from source motion as the Doppler effect.
remainingChecks: Add wavefront-spacing diagrams for approach/recession and distinguish emitted from observed frequency.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Both reflection and refraction apply to all wave types in this statement.

requirements.summary: Explain that waves can reflect.
remainingChecks: Validate longitudinal and transverse reflection examples.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain that waves can refract.
remainingChecks: Assess changing speed/wavelength with unchanged frequency, including normal incidence.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: The named spectrum regions and common free-space speed are explicit parts of the statement.

requirements.summary: Recognise light as part of the continuous spectrum including all seven named electromagnetic regions.
remainingChecks: Check all named regions without inventing physical gaps between bands.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Recognise their equal speed in free space.
remainingChecks: Check that the common vacuum speed is not applied unchanged inside materials.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Full-spectrum order and visible-colour order are both explicitly included.

requirements.summary: Order electromagnetic regions by decreasing wavelength and increasing frequency.
remainingChecks: Validate both order directions and comparisons across every region.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Order the visible colours consistently with wavelength and frequency.
remainingChecks: Add an independent colour-order/comparison task.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: All seven source bullets are tracked; paired applications stay named within their bullet requirement.

requirements.summary: Explain radio waves in broadcasting and communication.
remainingChecks: Validate property-to-use explanations for both broadcast and communication contexts.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain microwaves in cooking and satellite links.
remainingChecks: Validate absorption/heating and atmosphere/directional-link explanations separately.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain infrared in heaters and night-vision equipment.
remainingChecks: Calibrate energy absorption versus thermal detection; identify the night-vision mechanism.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain visible light in optical fibres and photography.
remainingChecks: Validate information pulses/TIR and image formation as separate applications.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain ultraviolet in fluorescent lamps.
remainingChecks: Assess absorption by the coating and emission of visible light without swapping wavelengths.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain X-rays for internal imaging, including medical imaging.
remainingChecks: Calibrate differential absorption/contrast as well as penetration.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain gamma rays for sterilising food and medical equipment.
remainingChecks: Assess microorganism damage and penetration through suitable packaging in both contexts.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Four named hazard bullets plus protective measures are tracked; these are curriculum explanations, not handling instructions.

requirements.summary: Explain excessive microwave exposure causing internal tissue heating.
remainingChecks: Validate the heating mechanism without wrongly requiring ionisation.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain excessive infrared exposure causing skin burns.
remainingChecks: Validate the radiation-to-heating link rather than a generic mutation claim.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain ultraviolet damage to surface cells and eyes, including blindness.
remainingChecks: Assess both surface-cell and eye hazards with appropriate protection.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain gamma exposure causing mutations and cancer.
remainingChecks: Validate cell/DNA damage explanations without implying every exposure causes cancer.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Describe simple protective measures matched to these risks.
remainingChecks: Calibrate radiation-specific shielding, time and distance or exposure barriers; not one universal shield.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Light’s transverse nature and boundary behaviours are distinct source demands.

requirements.summary: Recognise light as transverse.
remainingChecks: Validate classification without inventing a vibrating material medium.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Recognise that light reflects and refracts.
remainingChecks: Validate ray behaviour at normal and oblique incidence.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Angles are measured to the normal.

requirements.summary: Apply equal incidence and reflection angles.
remainingChecks: Validate diagram construction and surface-angle conversions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Actual drawing skill cannot be demonstrated by reading a finished diagram alone.

requirements.summary: Draw labelled reflection ray diagrams.
remainingChecks: Provide a drawing task and validate normal, angles and ray directions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Draw labelled refraction ray diagrams.
remainingChecks: Validate learner-drawn paths across both boundaries and their local normals.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Rectangular, semicircular and triangular shapes are all named practical contexts.

requirements.summary: Investigate refraction with a rectangular block.
remainingChecks: Validate full plan, observations and reconstructed ray angles.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Investigate refraction with a semicircular block.
remainingChecks: Add an independently checked radial-entry/flat-face ray diagram and practical results task.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Investigate refraction with a triangular prism.
remainingChecks: Add a two-face prism ray diagram and checked angle/deviation observations.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Know/use are local subdivisions; the notes specify entry from air for the displayed index relation.

requirements.summary: Know refractive index as sin i / sin r.
remainingChecks: Validate equation recall and conditions/angle definitions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use n = sin i / sin r.
remainingChecks: Calibrate inverse sine, degree mode and refractive-index targets.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: This practical specifically investigates glass index using a glass block.

requirements.summary: Investigate glass refractive index experimentally.
remainingChecks: Validate measured data, best-fit sine graph, uncertainty and axis choice.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Optical fibres and prisms are both named applications of total internal reflection.

requirements.summary: Explain total internal reflection guiding information through optical fibres.
remainingChecks: Validate core/cladding and incidence conditions without applying the material-to-air formula unchanged.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain total internal reflection in prisms.
remainingChecks: Add a ray-diagram task checking entry/exit and internal incidence separately.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Critical angle is measured inside the higher-index medium at refraction angle 90 degrees.

requirements.summary: Explain the meaning of critical angle.
remainingChecks: Assess a diagram at, below and above the critical angle.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Know/use local subdivisions; material-to-air condition is explicit in teaching.

requirements.summary: Know sin c = 1/n.
remainingChecks: Validate recall and boundary conditions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use sin c = 1/n.
remainingChecks: Calibrate both critical-angle and refractive-index targets.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Sound’s longitudinal nature and both boundary behaviours are included.

requirements.summary: Recognise sound as longitudinal.
remainingChecks: Assess particle vibration versus wave propagation using a sound representation.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Recognise sound reflection and refraction.
remainingChecks: Validate sound-specific examples of both reflection and speed-gradient refraction.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2-only numerical hearing-range statement, not a guarantee for every listener.

requirements.summary: Know the approximate 20–20 000 Hz human hearing range.
remainingChecks: Check both boundaries and kHz conversion in independent tasks.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2 practical; the source does not mandate one particular apparatus method.

requirements.summary: Investigate the speed of sound in air.
remainingChecks: Validate an independent plan/results task, path difference, timing and reflections.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2 display principle, distinct from measuring frequency in 3.27P.

requirements.summary: Explain how microphone and oscilloscope display a sound signal.
remainingChecks: Check pressure-to-electrical conversion, time base and that the trace is not particle motion.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2 practical; timing and frequency calculation both matter.

requirements.summary: Investigate sound frequency using an oscilloscope.
remainingChecks: Validate scaled trace reading, several-cycle intervals and repeated measurements.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2 pitch/frequency relation; amplitude is a different variable.

requirements.summary: Relate pitch to vibration frequency.
remainingChecks: Validate unequal-time-base trace comparisons without judging by raw cycle count.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2 loudness/amplitude relation; measurement and listening conditions require care.

requirements.summary: Relate loudness to vibration amplitude.
remainingChecks: Validate gain/scale controls and avoid inferring changed source amplitude from display height alone.
